LESSON: THE PREAMBLE OF THE CONSTITUTION OF KENYA.

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Governance
Topic 5.3: The Preamble of the Constitution of Kenya.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Preamble of the Constitution of Kenya., part of Governance in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How does the Kenyan Constitution enhance unity in the country?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Preamble of the Constitution of Kenya. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-Efficacy: A learner acquires effective communication skills as they create posters on key words of the preamble of

the Constitution of Kenya and display.

• Citizenship: A learner develops national and cultural identity skills as they discuss and list down the key words of the

preamble of the Constitution of Kenya and do presentations.

Values:
• Patriotism: Learners show readiness to defend their country by creating posters on key words of the preamble of the

Constitution of Kenya and display.

• Peace: Learners display calmness as they brainstorm on the meaning of a constitution and share.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Self -awareness: Learners engage with a resource person to interpret the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya.

• Social cohesion: Learners compose songs to sing on the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya.
